Regression-style tables of causal results

causal_table.Rd

Side-by-side tables of one or more intervene_membership() / intervene_effect() results, in the style of stargazer: estimates with significance stars, standard errors (or confidence intervals) below, and sample size, estimator and diagnostics in the footer. Results of both kinds can be combined; their rows are stacked and aligned by estimand.

Usage

causal_table(
  x,
  ...,
  format = c("text", "markdown", "latex", "html"),
  digits = 3,
  stars = c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001),
  ci = FALSE,
  level = 0.95,
  title = NULL,
  notes = NULL,
  labels = NULL,
  label = NULL,
  file = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'lcc_result'
lm_table(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'intervention_result'
lm_table(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'causal_table'
print(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'causal_table'
format(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'causal_table'
as.character(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A result, or a list of results (possibly named); for the print(), format() and as.character() methods, a causal_table.

...

More results; named arguments give the column headings. For the lm_table() methods, further arguments of causal_table().

format

"text" (default), "markdown", "latex" or "html".

digits

Number of decimal places.

stars

Significance thresholds for one, two and three stars (default c(0.05, 0.01, 0.001)); FALSE for none, TRUE for the default.

ci

Logical; show confidence intervals instead of standard errors.

level

Confidence level.

title, notes

Optional caption and extra notes.

labels

Optional column headings, one per result (default: argument or list names, else (1), (2), ...).

label

LaTeX label (\label{}).

file

Optional path; the table is also written there (UTF-8) and returned invisibly.

Value

The rendered table: an lm_table_output (when rendered by latentmixtures) or a causal_table; both are character strings that print as the table and are emitted as is in R Markdown. The print method returns x invisibly; format() and as.character() return a plain character string.

Details

lm_table() methods for lcc_result and intervention_result are registered with the latentmixtures::lm_table() generic when the namespace of latentmixtures is loaded, and tables are rendered by latentmixtures::lm_render() so they match the tables of latentmixtures. causal_table() is the same function under this package's own name and also works with versions of latentmixtures without lm_render() (it then uses its own renderer).

LaTeX output uses math for \(\Delta\), \(E[Y^{g_1}]\) and \(\psi\) and needs \usepackage{booktabs}. Footer rows: N, estimator, treatment and entropy for lcc_result; N, estimator, intervened exposures, interventions and the minimum propensity for intervention_result.

See also

intervene_membership(), intervene_effect(), latentmixtures::lm_table()

Examples

data(ace_study)
# \donttest{
# a table of two interventions on abuse and neglect (ace1, ace2), self-rated health
prevent <- intervene_effect(ace_study, outcome = health, exposures = ace1:ace8,
                               intervene = c(ace1, ace2),
                               confounders = c(age, female, parent_edu), g1 = setto(c(0, 0)))
#> Starting Julia ...
halve <- intervene_effect(ace_study, outcome = health, exposures = ace1:ace8,
                             intervene = c(ace1, ace2),
                             confounders = c(age, female, parent_edu), g1 = shift(0.5))
causal_table(`Prevent both` = prevent, `Halve both` = halve, format = "markdown")
#> |  | Prevent both | Halve both |
#> | :--- | :---: | :---: |
#> | E[Y^g1] | 78.965 | 77.864 |
#> |  | (0.305) | (0.256) |
#> | E[Y^g0] | 76.701 | 76.701 |
#> |  | (0.255) | (0.255) |
#> | Effect ψ | 2.264\*\*\* | 1.163\*\*\* |
#> |  | (0.208) | (0.094) |
#> | N | 2500 | 2500 |
#> | Estimator | AIPW | AIPW |
#> | Intervene | ace1, ace2 | ace1, ace2 |
#> | g1 | set to (0, 0) | shift 1→0 with probability 0.5 |
#> | g0 | natural course | natural course |
#> | Min. propensity | 0.0050 | 0.0050 |
#> 
#> *\* p < .05, \*\* p < .01, \*\*\* p < .001; Standard errors in parentheses.*  
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".tex")
causal_table(`Prevent both` = prevent, `Halve both` = halve, format = "latex", file = f)
latentmixtures::lm_table(prevent, halve, format = "markdown", ci = TRUE)
#> |  | (1) | (2) |
#> | :--- | :---: | :---: |
#> | E[Y^g1] | 78.965 | 77.864 |
#> |  | [78.367, 79.563] | [77.363, 78.365] |
#> | E[Y^g0] | 76.701 | 76.701 |
#> |  | [76.202, 77.201] | [76.202, 77.201] |
#> | Effect ψ | 2.264\*\*\* | 1.163\*\*\* |
#> |  | [1.855, 2.673] | [0.978, 1.348] |
#> | N | 2500 | 2500 |
#> | Estimator | AIPW | AIPW |
#> | Intervene | ace1, ace2 | ace1, ace2 |
#> | g1 | set to (0, 0) | shift 1→0 with probability 0.5 |
#> | g0 | natural course | natural course |
#> | Min. propensity | 0.0050 | 0.0050 |
#> 
#> *\* p < .05, \*\* p < .01, \*\*\* p < .001; 95% confidence intervals in brackets.*  
# }
